basis: Juvenile lens cataracts define the disease; arrhythmia in 14/19 (~74%) supports cardiac involvement despite the nonsyndromic designation.
Anterior temporal neurodegeneration causes progressive loss of semantic knowledge; visual agnosia is cerebral, not intrinsic eye damage.
Adenoma originates in the parathyroid endocrine gland; systemic consequences of hyperparathyroidism are not established for this tumour subtype.
Inherited marrow failure defines Fanconi anemia; developmental delay is reported in 20/20. Skeletal and renal anomalies lack subtype-specific frequencies.
Undifferentiated carcinoma originates in the stomach; metastatic organ involvement is not intrinsic to the concept.
Hereditary corticospinal disease; fixed lower-limb contractures occur in 80-99% and muscle atrophy in 8/10. Optic atrophy is only occasional.
Inherited multiple cutaneous keratoacanthomas cause persistent nodules and ulcerative skin lesions; mucosal involvement is not characteristic.
Primary systemic fungal infection; pulmonary tissue infection occurs commonly (>30%) across the major endemic mycoses. Other damaged organs vary by fungus.
Scrotal cancers predominantly arise in scrotal skin, usually as squamous carcinoma; this supports a cutaneous axis despite reproductive-site classification.
Polymicrogyria, microcephaly and pyramidal tract abnormalities establish CNS disease; respiratory insufficiency is a defining component.
Varicella-zoster infection directly causes dermatitis of eyelid skin; eyelids fall within the ocular axis.
Inherited sialic-acid biosynthesis disorder causes degenerative skeletal myopathy. Hypothyroidism is separately diagnosed; cardiomyopathy occurs in only 1-4%.
Mansonella nematode infection; eosinophilia, pruritus and arthralgia do not establish common direct damage to additional organs across the group.
Defining radial/thumb malformations affect skeleton; hypospadias affects urethra; maxillary diastema is a named dental feature. Dermatoglyphics imply no skin damage.
Inherited epidermal hyperkeratosis of palms and soles; associated malignancies are separate diseases and uncommon.
Autoimmune connective-tissue overlap commonly affects joints and muscle; visceral involvement varies across constituent overlap syndromes.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures; structural laryngomalacia affects 26/35 (~74%). Feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
T/B-cell deficiency defines SCID; cutaneous granulomas are annotated in 30-79%. Bronchiectasis, infections and autoimmune hemolytic anemia are separate diseases.
Facial spasm is a disorder of facial motor control; associated hyporeflexia supports neurologic localization without evidence of primary muscle disease.
Congenital cerebellar neurodevelopmental disorder; oculomotor findings do not establish intrinsic eye damage. Isolated renal and skeletal reports lack reliable prevalence.
Immune-mediated Crohn inflammation directly damages the jejunum; extraintestinal diseases are not established by this localized concept.
Progressive myoclonus epilepsy with ataxia; structural scoliosis occurs in 6/6 reported patients, supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Abnormal lymphocyte cytokine production drives eosinophilia and immune-mediated tissue injury; persistent cutaneous involvement occurs in roughly 70-80%.
Chronic suppurative infection of the middle ear with tympanic membrane perforation directly damages the ear.
Immune large-vessel vasculitis; skin ulcers and arthritis are each annotated 30-79%. Renal artery stenosis is vascular; stroke and retinopathy are occasional.
